correctness.rationale: The exact stated pure multiplication yields H with determinant -2xyz/(uvw), so the product image equals 3D quaternion subspace U, forcing pure orthogonal automorphisms diag(R,epsilon). Orientation of U gives R in SO(3), and det H≠0 implies epsilon=1, hence centralizer in SO(3). For anisotropic parameters skew K has axis kappa with component signs (b-c,c-a,a-b); an oblique non-half-turn would require S=alpha I+beta kk^T, impossible from zero diagonal and strictly negative off-diagonal entries. With exactly two equal parameters the kappa half-turn commutes; with all distinct, positive diagonal D symmetrizes H with simple real spectrum and kappa with nonzero components, so commuting half-turn would force D scalar and a=b=c, contradiction. Isotropic centralizer is O(2), and ell/sqrt(d) removes d. Independently verified DH=H^T D and sample half-turn behavior for (1,1,1),(1,1,4),(1,4,9), supporting but not replacing analytic reasoning.
